claims.text: The baseline material consists of approximately 5 nm carbon-supported PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution nanoparticles.
The baseline nanoparticles have a moderate Ru content.
Increasing Ru content under ethanol-oxidation conditions creates additional partially oxidized Ru sites.
The partially oxidized Ru sites form adjacent to Pt or Pd centers.
Partially oxidized Ru sites modulate the adsorption energies of reactive ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Oxygenated Ru species promote hydroxyl adsorption and water activation.
The Ru-derived oxygenated species synergistically assist Pt/Pd centers in cleaving C–C bonds.
Pt/Pd sites further oxidize and remove carbonaceous intermediates.
Removal of carbonaceous intermediates reduces catalyst poisoning and increases turnover frequency.
Increasing Ru content above baseline will lower the ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Increasing Ru content above baseline will increase ethanol-oxidation current density.
Increasing Ru content above baseline will reduce the coverage of poisoning intermediates.
Increasing Ru content above baseline will improve durability over repeated electrocatalytic cycles.
The proposed mechanism should operate at 0.4–0.8 V versus RHE in either acidic or alkaline electrolyte.
The hypothesis should hold up to approximately 80 °C for particles below approximately 10 nm and Ru contents from 0 to 15 at.%.
Large particle-size changes or extreme Ru loadings may introduce additional structural and electronic effects.
Other multimetallic systems provide strong evidence that Ru-oxide sites facilitate C–C bond cleavage.
Direct confirmation of the proposed Ru mechanism in PtPdRhRuIrOs is limited.
The hypothesis is falsified if increasing Ru produces neither a difference in partial Ru oxidation nor a measurable improvement in C–C cleavage or stability relative to baseline.

contradictions.description: The intervention changes Ru content, whereas the baseline is described as having the same nominal composition but lower Ru content. If nominal composition includes elemental fractions, these conditions cannot both be true; the baseline should instead be described as containing the same elements with a specified lower Ru fraction and compensating changes in other elements.
